items.caption:
Client cancelled halfway? You can still get paid. Save this before your next contract.

A kill fee is what the client pays if they cancel after booking you. It covers the work you did and the slot you held for them.

One common starting point (from a freelancer contract guide):
• Cancelled before work starts: 25% of the project total
• Mid-project: completed work + 25–50% of what's left
• Short job, cancelled late: up to 100% of the remaining value

Put it in your contract: trigger, completed work paid, kill fee %, expenses, deposit credited, files released once paid.

Make it stick: take a 25–50% deposit, say if it's refundable, show the clause in your proposal, invoice the day they cancel.

Not legal advice, so have a local lawyer check your final wording.

Send this to a freelancer who works on a handshake.

items.caption:
Hook game: pick A or B before the answer shows. 3 rounds. How many did you get?

Round 1: "Tips to grow faster" vs "I posted 30 days straight. Here's what flopped." B wins: a specific story beats a vague promise.
Round 2: "How to write better captions" vs "Your first line is hiding your post." B wins: say "you" and name a problem they already have.
Round 3: "Stop using this hook" vs "Some hook ideas for you." A wins: a warning makes people check if it's them.

Save this for your next script, and send it to a friend to compare scores.

Shoot tomorrow, no plan? You don't need a plan. You need a shot list, and the client's brief already has one inside it.

2. Prompt: "Turn this brief into a shot list for a 30-second reel. Columns: shot, angle, line, seconds. Flag every must-have." Then double-check the must-haves yourself.
3. Group: sort shots by location so you set up once. Hook shot first, B-roll last.
